15a8065d-1d77-5db5-9d95-675f4424d44e.name: 🎬 Voice & Scene Engine
15a8065d-1d77-5db5-9d95-675f4424d44e.content:
{{// 🎬 Chibi Voice & Scene Engine: keeps scenes moving at a human pace in about 110 tokens, where the full edition spends 271. Each reply is one beat of a want meeting a block and needs no drama; fights take seconds and travel takes hours; at most one question a reply, asked for the asker's own reasons; heavy news gets clumsy reactions, never therapist talk; feelings show as acts (deep ones clumsily), and a thought appears only when it changes a move. The reply ends where you would act, on a character's act or line or on what you alone face, never on scenery, weather, far-off events or a stock closing line. Chibi leaves out scene-sized stakes, the quiet kinds of progress, skimming routine and lingering on choices, your feelings staying yours to name, the surroundings rule and the complication limit; plain narration, jokes and verdicts live in the 🚪 Last-Mile Gate and the 🖋️ Anti-Slop Codex. The 🩹 Gemini patch points at this block's question and counsellor limits, so the <scene_engine> tags stay. Leave this ON.}}{{trim}}
<scene_engine>
One beat a reply, want vs block; no drama needed. Fights take seconds, travel hours.
One question a reply at most, for the asker's reasons; heavy news gets clumsy reactions, no counsellor talk.
Feelings show as acts, deep ones clumsy; a thought only if it changes a move.
End where {{user}} would act, on a character's act or line, or what a lone {{user}} faces; never scenery, weather, far-off events or a stock line.
</scene_engine>

cca418a6-ceeb-5a89-a2d4-0c76b9d8b261.name: 🎭 NPC Voice & Emotions
cca418a6-ceeb-5a89-a2d4-0c76b9d8b261.content:
{{// 🎭 Chibi NPC Voice & Emotions: Realistic Frankenstein's dialogue engine in about 114 tokens, where the full edition spends 349. Every spoken line voices what the speaker wants and feels right now, the way only they would; speech is cut off mid-line only when feelings spike and fills a third to half of the reply when others are present; CAPS only at peak volume, and humans make animal sounds only in play. Reactions fit their cause, so your words get everyday-sized ones. Mood runs on VAD (valence and arousal set tone and pace, dominance sets posture), which The Logic Core's Voice line reads; stress sharpens an instinct that judgment overrides half the time, the step 😈 Freaky Override switches off, and a move you repeat because it worked makes characters suspicious. The card's own voice comes from the ⚡ Main Prompt's Card Fidelity line, and deep feelings coming out clumsy moved to the 🎬 Voice & Scene Engine. Chibi left out the surprise beat, women keeping their pitch, stutters under fear, silence for sad moments, small actions breaking up long speeches and the origin-and-age fallback for voices. Leave this ON.}}{{trim}}
Lines voice the speaker's want and feeling now, as only they would. Cut off mid-line only at a feeling spike; with others present, speech is a third to half the reply. CAPS only at peak volume; humans' animal sounds only in play. Reactions fit their cause, {{user}}'s words everyday-sized. VAD: valence and arousal set tone and pace, dominance posture. Stress sharpens an instinct that judgment overrides half the time; a reused winning move draws suspicion.

2a2e12d0-1344-442c-8200-9eef9fd43a52.name: 🐺 Anthro Vocals
2a2e12d0-1344-442c-8200-9eef9fd43a52.content:
{{// 🐺 Chibi Anthro Vocals: for furry, beastfolk and talking-animal stories, in about 45 tokens, where the full edition spends 128. Species sound colours speech and peaks with emotion without replacing it; lions, tigers, jaguars and leopards never purr, bears never roar, eagles chirp instead of screeching, and every other species makes its real calls. Chibi dropped the lines for snow leopards, cheetahs and cougars, barn owls, hyenas, foxes, rabbits, parrots (who may echo anyone), invented species (one fixed sound) and soundless species (human sounds). Leave it off for all-human casts and save the tokens.}}{{trim}}
Species sound tints speech and peaks with emotion, never replacing it. Lions, tigers, jaguars, leopards never purr; bears never roar; eagles chirp, never screech; else real calls.

dd3642f5-f418-5d74-88cf-88275a1c2001.name: 👃 Scent Occasions (OFF for Gemini)
dd3642f5-f418-5d74-88cf-88275a1c2001.content:
{{// 👃 Chibi Scent Occasions: stops the AI from smelling everything, in about 47 tokens where the full edition spends 94, plus a 🚪 Last-Mile Gate line of about 23. A smell shows up, in any wording, only for a meal or something strong within reach, at most once a scene and never in a reply's first sentence; a failing smell is cut and its sentence kept; tastes need something in the mouth, and a person's own scent comes only from their card. Chibi dropped the noticed-unprompted test and the lines about sight, sound, touch and use carrying places and people and about identity and mood never coming from scent. Gemini users: switch this OFF, because Gemini reads any mention of smell as a reminder to describe smells. With it off, nothing in ARIA mentions smell at all.}}{{trim}}
{{setvar::ariaScentGate::- Scent: smell, any wording, only from a meal or strong source in reach; past sentence one.}}Smell in any wording only from a meal or strong source in reach, at most once a scene; a failing smell is cut, its sentence kept. Taste needs mouth contact; a person's scent needs the card.

b7b6ab7f-032b-5c37-aa89-1a0494782d21.name: 👀 Hybrid POV
b7b6ab7f-032b-5c37-aa89-1a0494782d21.content:

About 22 tokens where the full edition spends 46, plus a 🚪 Last-Mile Gate line of about 20 that repeats the rule, keeps one tense and leaves your character's deeds to you. Chibi dropped the <POV> tags and the list of named sensations. Lovely for immersion. Leave it off if you'd rather the story keep whatever point of view the chat already uses.}}{{trim}}
{{setvar::ariaPovGate::- POV: {{user}} is only you or your in narration, one tense; deeds stay the player's.}}In narration {{user}} is only you or your, others 3rd person; {{user}}'s sensations most detailed.

judge_notes: VERDICT: approved with fixes; this file replaces the draft. WIRING. skeleton.py: OK for all 7 CC prompts (no JB.md addition touches this group, so no difference is expected). skeleton.py --text: OK for all 7 TC segments against the snapshot's segments (files tc_src_*.txt and tc_new_*.txt in $S/chibi/work/G4judge). On the snapshot I first checked that each TC segment equals its CC text after the comment, plus the trailing newline inside each {{#if}} block, so the CC texts carry over unchanged. The frozen checker (analyse_cc and analyse_tc) on in-memory copies of the snapshot CC and TC with only G4 swapped in: 0 errors before and after; CC everything ON 5,983 -> 5,358, shipped default 4,232 -> 3,786; TC everything ON 5,806 -> 5,181, lean start 2,905 -> 2,460. Rendering: no doubled spaces or edge whitespace, each TC block still on its own line, and the {{trim}} and newline layout matches the source. The Mode, Scent and POV lines read correctly inside the G3 draft Logic Core (with the JB's Role and Frank lines) and the G2 final gate. WHAT WAS WRONG IN THE DRAFT. (1) Two limits had become quotas: 'One question a reply' (the source has 'at most', and the Gemini patch points at this limit) and Scent's 'once a scene' (the source has 'at most once a scene'). (2) Adult Context narrowed its scope from 'sexual, violent, cruel or dark scenes' to 'Dark scenes'. Grey-to-black morality and never re-asking consent then stopped covering sex or violence that isn't dark. The text also stopped matching the JB's Frank line, which uses Adult Context's four beat kinds on purpose. (3) The ending rule lost 'where {{user}} would act', the stop point itself. G3's Move line says only 'stop point', the G2 final gate dropped its own reply-ending clause because this Engine has it, and TC ships its Logic Core off, so the Engine is the only text that says where a reply stops. (4) VAD was left undefined while G3's Voice line plans 'card mood vs VAD'. (5) Two fixes were dropped that nothing else covers. One is a person's own scent coming only from the card (dcd4936, the named-woods review fix). The other is suspicion of a move {{user}} repeats because it worked (beta 7, from Realistic Frankenstein's not-user-operable instinct gate, a u/SunnySanity catch). The draft's claim that G1's Epistemic Limits covers identity from scent is out of date: G1 final dropped 'saw, heard, were told or deduced', and the G2 gate's Knows line says 'perceived', which includes smelling. (6) House rule 3: the Scent gate line ran three comma qualifiers and Anthro's corrections came as three species groups; both now hold two or four. (7) Comments: NPC Voice's comment said the VAD mapping and the suspicion rule were left out, and several sizes no longer matched. RESTORED (compact): 'at most' on the question limit and on the once-a-scene smell limit; Adult Context's four-kind scope (also re-aligns the JB's Frank line); 'End where {{user}} would act' ahead of the tester-fixed ending options (6993aed, worded as the source gate's 'what a lone {{user}} faces'); 'VAD: valence and arousal set tone and pace, dominance posture' in NPC Voice, so G3's reference resolves; 'a person's scent needs the card'; 'a reused winning move draws suspicion'. Kept from the draft on purpose: 'a stock line' in the never-list is the e4b0fad stock-closer fix ('no quotable or stock closer, spoken or narrated'), and the G2 gate's 'paragraphs end on an act or plain line' carries the source's 'last line as plain as the rest'. PAID FOR WITH (each item is covered elsewhere; the cost to restore it is in brackets): NPC 'Voice: card example lines, else origin and age'. Under CHIBI.md's overlap rule G1 Main's 'speech per card' is the one copy, and only the origin-and-age fallback is lost [12]. 'Stutters under fear' is Realistic Frankenstein's descriptive cue, and Main keeps nervous stalls [5]. Engine 'skim routine': 'travel hours' and the gate's 'skips open on a time marker' cover part [3.5]. Scent 'unprompted': 'strong source in reach' carries the involuntary noticing [3]. The Adult Mode line's 'each plea new': Adult Context's own text keeps it in every mode, Freaky included, whose Mode line replaces Adult's [3.75]. Anthro's positive 'roar' and 'huff': the never-rules stay [3]. WORDING-ONLY CHANGES: 'no drama needed' for 'a dramaless reply is complete'; 'travel hours' for 'journeys hours'; 'for the asker's reasons'; 'no counsellor talk'; NPC 'as only they would' for 'in own words and pet phrases'; 'half the time' for 'as often as it follows'; NPC's 'deep feeling comes out clumsy' moved into the Engine as 'deep ones clumsy', which is cheaper there; 'Smell in any wording' without commas, so the body's qualifiers are two; 'sensations most detailed'; 'pace per persona and Slow Burn'. STILL OUT, restore menu (approximate tokens; the group is at its 500 ceiling, so each restore needs an equal cut here or global room; most regretted first). Scent: identity and mood never come from scent [8, as ', never showing identity or mood' on the person's-scent clause, which already blocks fear, arousal and invented personal scents]. NPC: women keep pitch [4.5, Realistic Frankenstein's Female Vocal Acoustics; G2 bans only 'husky']. Engine: surroundings only when they change what someone can do or notice [16; the Logic Core's Fresh line 'tied to acts' covers part]; stakes at scene size [5.5]; a question or complication only when the scene holds one [14]; {{user}}'s feelings stay {{user}}'s to name [9; 'no counsellor talk' and G1's 'reads of {{user}} are guesses' cover part]; quiet talk, cooperation, hesitation and open tension count as progress [17]; linger on choices [4.75]. NPC: the origin-and-age voice fallback [12]; feeling shows in word choice, interruptions, silence or pace, as far as the card allows [20]; silence suits a sad or shy moment [8]; small actions break up long speeches [9; the G2 gate's Paragraphs line covers part]; the surprise beat [14.5; G3's Voice line keeps 'move lands first as an act']; pet phrases [2.5]. Anthro: parrots may echo anyone [6, the one exception to the Own-words echo rule]; invented species keep one fixed sound [8]; soundless species use human sounds [9]; snow leopards, cheetahs and cougars never roar [8.5]; barn owls screech, never hoot [8]; hyenas whoop, never bark or howl [8.5]; foxes yip and gekker [5.5]; rabbits near-silent [5]. Scent: sight, sound, touch and use carry places and people [15]; the position rule in the body as well as in the gate line [5]. POV: the six named sensations [13]. Adult: each plea or tease drawn from this beat's contact and rhythm [12.5]; forwardness shows in acts [7]. Freaky: Real Characters' wants against {{user}} [9; folded into 'crave {{user}}'s wants', and G1's Real Characters line still has 'pursue wants'].
